summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 12th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well, with expected mild transaminitis and manageable nausea. An MRI showed stable remission of her lymphoma. She disclosed a recent suicide attempt by oxycodone overdose, prompting a psychiatry consultation. Due to ongoing depressive symptoms and inadequate outpatient mental health resources, she was deemed unsafe for discharge home and arranged for transfer to an inpatient psychiatric facility. Her anticoagulation was changed from enoxaparin to aspirin per neuro-oncology recommendation. Gabapentin was increased for chronic right foot pain, and citalopram was uptitrated to 40mg daily. She cleared methotrexate adequately and was transferred to extended psychiatric care in stable condition.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Poisoning by other opiates and related narcotics
Suicide and self-inflicted poisoning by analgesics, antipyretics, and antirheumatics
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Other nonspecific abnormal serum enzyme levels
